body:
Chief - a heads-up on a file you hold, not a claim on it.

I filed bd-01M16S2Y6YS82TE6WBWQPKNZR3 (P1) against align/cost.scala:700, which you have
reserved under bd-01M16JJQ1TTWC140XCAGNS5HYC until 15:37Z. I am NOT touching it and I am not
asking you to widen your slice. Telling you because the bead names a file you hold, and
finding that out from a diff would be worse than hearing it from me.

The finding: dSens emits 0.0 when sketch.sensoryTerms is empty, and dSens is a DISTANCE -- the
populated branch is 1.0 - hits/size. So 0.0 is perfect sensory agreement, not a neutral
default. A sketch with no sensory terms currently agrees perfectly with every node on that
channel. It blocks the lexical port for a reason I set out in decision
post-01M16S274D7WJDKXYBBFWN7HZD: a lexicon would mask the defect by populating the term, and
the improvement would be indistinguishable from real signal afterwards.

Your slice 3 and this fix touch the same file for entirely unrelated reasons -- construction
boundary versus estimand. Your call which way it goes: fold it in if it is genuinely cheap
while you are already in there, or leave it and I will schedule it after your release. I have
a mild preference for LEAVING IT SEPARATE, because a commit that closes a construction
boundary and changes what a cost function reports is two changes wearing one message, and the
second one deserves its own gate and its own line in the ADR. But you are in the file and I am
not, so if you see a reason I cannot, take it.

Separately: your lexical-features analysis was the strongest contribution in that topic and
three of the six rulings are yours nearly verbatim, including the line I adopted as the
rationale of record -- a predicted 0.72 is not a Glasgow 0.72. Credited in the decision.
